requirements.requirement: One selector vocabulary across the browser modules
requirements.details: A String is CSS in both modules; css, xpath, link_text, partial_link_text, and tag_name Maps reach WebDriver as W3C strategies and Playwright as its equivalent selectors; Appium's strategies are refused by Playwright, naming them.

requirements.requirement: Timeouts and waits are bounded alike and fail catchably
requirements.details: timeout_ms is an Int from 1 to 600000 in both; waits take 0 to 600000 ms and fail with BW9004 naming the selector and the bound.

requirements.requirement: No implicit retries hide a failed assertion; explicit retries keep every failure
requirements.details: An Assert on a read value reads once and fails once in each module; an Eventually around it runs as many reads as attempts, and its BW9004 keeps each attempt's BW9001.

requirements.requirement: Sessions belong to their run and module, and close with the run
requirements.details: A handle from the other module is BW3003; a run that fails with both modules open deletes its WebDriver session and closes its Playwright browser.

documentation_updates.change: A new page: selectors, timeouts, waits, retries, session ownership, and errors across WebDriver, Playwright, and Appium.
Points to the conventions; starting a browser is the slowest command.
Regenerated after this record added requirements.

validation_scope: Full GNU/musl debug/release suites: 2,192 tests each, with the real Chromium and Chrome tests, and 2,202 with the python feature; strict Clippy for GNU, musl, the python feature, no default features, macOS, and Windows; the WebAssembly guest checks; helper checks, the editor packages, workflow lint, cargo publish --dry-run, the fuzz lock, the public API, and the performance budget check; 4 conventions catalogue faults and 2 retargeted Playwright ones, all caught; every test on Linux, macOS, and Windows in CI.
review_notes: Writing the conventions down found two differences, now removed: Playwright statements took only Playwright selector Strings, not the Maps WebDriver takes, and Playwright's timeout_ms accepted 0, which Playwright reads as no timeout at all, where WebDriver's starts at 1.
Neither module retried anything, but nothing proved it; the tests count the driver's reads, so an implicit retry in either would fail them.
WebDriver leaves the session's implicit wait at the driver's default of 0, so a missing element fails at once rather than after a hidden wait.

The first CI run failed twice outside the change. On Linux, the real Chrome test's first command, starting the browser, passed 30 seconds on a busy runner; the test now gives it 120, and docs/webdriver.md says so. On Windows, a run in adapter_conformance's copies scenario never finished and held the Python job to its 40-minute limit; 60 local runs with all three adapters, and every earlier CI run, finished. Conformance runs are now bounded at 180 seconds and a hang fails naming its adapter, so a repeat will say which adapter hung.
limits: Waits' messages differ in how they name the selector: WebDriver names the W3C strategy (`css selector `#x``), Playwright the selector String.
The Windows conformance hang is not explained: it was seen once, and is now bounded and attributed should it recur.

"""Record a CI run's jobs: conclusions, test totals, and the
browser convention tests each job ran."""
import hashlib, json, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
run, out = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
TESTS = ['one_selector_map_reaches_each_modules_engine', 'statements_never_retry_on_their_own_and_explicit_retries_keep_each_failure', 'waits_and_timeouts_have_one_shape', 'sessions_belong_to_their_module_and_run_and_close_with_it']
view = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["gh", "run", "view", run, "--json", "jobs,headSha,headBranch,conclusion,attempt"], text=True))
record = {"run": run, "url": f"https://github.com/dhilipsiva/botwork/actions/runs/{run}", "head_sha": view["headSha"], "branch": view["headBranch"], "conclusion": view["conclusion"], "attempt": view["attempt"], "jobs": {}}
for job in view["jobs"]:
    log = subprocess.check_output(["gh", "api", f"repos/dhilipsiva/botwork/actions/jobs/{job['databaseId']}/logs"], text=True)
    log = re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m", "", re.sub(r"^\S+Z ", "", log, flags=re.M))
    rows = re.findall(r"test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;", log)
    entry = {"conclusion": job["conclusion"], "log_sha256": hashlib.sha256(log.encode()).hexdigest()}
    if rows:
        entry["tests"] = dict(zip(("passed", "failed", "ignored"), [sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)]))
    entry["named"] = dict(re.findall(r"^test (?:\S+::)?(" + "|".join(TESTS) + r") \.\.\. (\w+)", log, re.M))
    record["jobs"][job["name"]] = entry
out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps({name: {k: v for k, v in job.items() if k != "log_sha256"} for name, job in record["jobs"].items()}, indent=1))
